header.name: Market Design
header.description: The theory of auctions has been one of the most important successes of applied game theory. It has become a central institution for resource allocation in real world markets; instrumental in allocating resources as varied as natural resources, spectrum rights, electricity generating capacity and more. This course aims to prepare the students to be able to analyze auctions and internet marketplaces using tools from economics and game theory.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students can analyze bidder behavior in standard auction formats for selling single and multiple units of a good.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students understand and be able to work with the analystical framework of mechanism design which is the underlying science.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students can discuss the most important considerations that go into practical auction design.

lecture_topics: Auctions in a Private Values Environment
Mechanism Design and Revenue Maximizing Auctions
Matching Markets and Deferred Acceptance Algorithm

resources.title: Vijay Krishna, Auction Theory, Academic Press
Paul Milgrom, Putting Auction Theory to Work, Cambridge University Press
Cramton, Shoham, Steinberg, Combinatorial Auctions, MIT Press
